t: Practical skills: uncertainty, graphs and estimation

practical-skills-uncertainty-graphs-and-: A newton, a joule, a watt: what are they actually made of?
newtonian-physics-part-2: A runner finishes a lap exactly where she started. What was her average velocity?
newtonian-physics-part-3: Hold a heavy bag still for ten minutes and your arms ache. How much work have you done on the bag?
newtonian-physics-part-4: Whirl a ball on a string in a circle. Is anything pulling it outwards?
newtonian-physics-part-5: Keep cooling a gas in a sealed box. At what temperature would its pressure reach zero?
newtonian-physics-part-6: Under the same Sun, beach sand gets scorching while the sea stays cool. Why?
component-2-electricity-and-the-universe: A lamp glows while charge flows through it. Does any of the charge get used up on the way?
electricity-and-the-universe-part-2: One dead bulb can put out a whole string of lights, yet home lamps work on their own. Why?
electricity-and-the-universe-part-3: A discharging capacitor never quite empties. So what sets how fast it gets close?
electricity-and-the-universe-part-4: Astronauts float on the space station. How much weaker is Earth's gravity up there?
electricity-and-the-universe-part-5: Sing a higher note. Does the sound reach the far side of the room any sooner?
electricity-and-the-universe-part-6: Double a satellite's orbital radius. How many times longer does one orbit then take?
component-3-light-nuclei-and-options: Two corks bob on the same ripple, half a wavelength apart. How do their movements compare?
light-nuclei-and-options-part-2: Two slits, a laser and a ruler: how can stripes on a wall measure a wavelength far thinner than a hair?
light-nuclei-and-options-part-3: Experiments in the early 1800s convinced physicists light is a wave. Which experiment made them think again?
light-nuclei-and-options-part-4: How can a sheet of paper and a strip of aluminium reveal what a radioactive source emits?
light-nuclei-and-options-part-5: An electron meets its antimatter twin and both vanish. What comes out, and why never just one thing?
light-nuclei-and-options-part-6: Switch on a current in a wire just above a compass. Which way does the needle turn, and why?
light-nuclei-and-options-part-7: Drop a strong magnet down a copper pipe and it falls in slow motion. Why?
